1924, May
FR. SOLANUS, NOTEBOOK NO. 1
Page 9 Cont.
May 8 "Good News To-day!" Exclaimed Fr. Guard. This A.M. His niece and god-child L.F. 18 of Brooklyn had been giving family anxiety through, what was feared, blindly loving a non-catholic Sailor from St. Louis (W.M. ) Like all good girls in such friendships she hoped to convert him - bringing him to the Monastery and enquiring about the S.M. A. May 4th she returned and enrolled him as perpetual member May 4th, sending him certificate etc. to St. L. Everything was returned this A.M. - Spell seems broken and danger feared by family and (real) friends averted. L.F. seems resigned.
9th Catherine O'Mara 24 - 552 W. 132nd St. restless nights since 11 years old - often in terrible fits. Enrolled perpetually To-day
12th Veronica McTaggart (45) 58 E. 130 St. drinking for 20 years, at times on Ward's Island seldom sober more than a few weeks, away from husband - little boy neglected - Enrolled for two years; Her Sister Ellen anxiously solicitous about her.
13 Mary Lyons (28) hoplessly cancerous with one breast amputated 18 months and dislocated (?) hipp, on Wards Island - having as nurse received a kick from an inmate of the asylum about 3 years ago, en- rolled to-day for one year (Miss McBride)
(10 p.m.) Fr. S. Visited her this evening. -
May 15th goes again accompied by J. Singer who cures cancer - Singer leaves his remedy - Annerita
Page 10 May 16 Death Bed Brings Sacraments. Andrew J. Byrnes 52 139 Quincy St. N.Y. away from home 3 months, drinking ocassionally and negligent to-ward dependents was enrolled for one year in hopes of information, February 29th. To-day reported to have died May 8th in Kings Co. Hospital after receiving all Sacraments -- his friends with him. & served Mass faithfully as a boy for 7 yrs. -- Raves about loved pas- tor of boy-hood His family friends much appreciative and grateful to God for favorable death.
